```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = '#>', message = FALSE)
```

An upstream API revision can break one operation while the rest stay healthy.
specmill gives you three ways to handle it. This guide runs each one against a
small schema so you can see what specmill reads and decides at every step. Every
evaluated example runs when this guide is built and contacts no service.

| You want to | Use | What happens to existing code |
|---|---|---|
| Wait for upstream to fix the contract | **Defer** (`deferrals = list(enroll = ...)`) | Kept. Never deleted. |
| Stop wrapping the operation on purpose | **Skip** (`selection: exclude`) | An eligible wrapper is removed. |
| Wrap it now | **Fix** the schema or a copy of it | Generated normally. |

The reference for the deferral lifecycle is in
[Routine maintenance and CI](maintenance.html#defer-a-changed-contract-that-does-not-validate-yet).
This guide is the worked example.

## 1. The project and the schema

The project has one service and one schema. `GET /bad` has a `200` response with
no `description`, which Swagger 2.0 requires.

```{r project}
root <- tempfile('deferral-demo-')
dir.create(file.path(root, 'R'), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines('request_helper <- function(...) list(...)', file.path(root, 'R/helper.R'))
writeLines(c('config_version: 1', 'services: [service.yml]'), file.path(root, 'specmill.yml'))
writeLines(c(
  'id: demo',
  'schemas: {files: [api.yml]}',
  'helper: request_helper',
  'names:',
  '  GET /good: demo_good',
  '  GET /bad: demo_bad',
  '  GET /health: demo_health'
), file.path(root, 'service.yml'))

write_schema <- function(bad_description = NULL) {
  response <- if (is.null(bad_description)) {
    '        "200": {schema: {type: object}}'
  } else {
    paste0('        "200": {description: ', bad_description, ', schema: {type: object}}')
  }
  writeLines(c(
    'swagger: "2.0"',
    'info: {title: Demo, version: "1"}',
    'host: api.example.org',
    'schemes: [https]',
    'paths:',
    '  /good:',
    '    get:',
    '      operationId: good',
    '      responses:',
    '        "200": {description: OK}',
    '  /bad:',
    '    get:',
    '      operationId: bad',
    '      responses:',
    response,
    '  /health:',
    '    get:',
    '      operationId: health',
    '      responses:',
    '        "200": {description: OK}'
  ), file.path(root, 'api.yml'))
}
write_schema()
cat(readLines(file.path(root, 'api.yml')), sep = '\n')
```

## 2. What specmill sees

specmill reads the file twice, with different jobs. The parser translates
operations. The validator checks the whole document against the official
OpenAPI JSON Schema.

```{r parse}
parsed <- specmill::read_operations(file.path(root, 'api.yml'))
names(parsed$operations)
length(parsed$diagnostics)
```

The parser accepts all three operations. The validator does not:

```{r validate}
validation <- specmill::validate_schema(file.path(root, 'api.yml'))
validation$status
validation$reason
data.frame(
  level = vapply(validation$findings, `[[`, character(1), 'level'),
  scope = vapply(validation$findings, `[[`, character(1), 'scope'),
  operation = vapply(validation$findings, function(x) x$keys[[1]], character(1)),
  message = vapply(validation$findings, `[[`, character(1), 'message')
)
```

The finding is `scope: operation` and names exactly one operation. That is what
makes it deferrable. A document-level finding, or an unreadable file, blocks the
whole run and cannot be deferred.

## 3. The blocked plan

Plan is read-only. With default strict validation, the failing operation is
reported as `unsupported` and the run cannot be applied:

```{r blocked}
plan <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
blocked <- plan$diagnostics[[1]]
unlist(blocked[c('id', 'status', 'classification', 'code', 'reason', 'guidance')])
```

`apply` refuses to continue until you choose one of the three paths below:

```{r blocked-apply}
tryCatch(
  specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply'),
  error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), '\n')
)
```

## 4. Defer

Enrollment is explicit. The key is `<service id> <METHOD> <path>` and the reason
is one line.

```{r enroll-plan}
enroll <- list(enroll = c('demo GET /bad' = 'Response lacks a description'))
plan <- specmill::generate_client(
  root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan', deferrals = enroll
)
data.frame(
  operation = names(plan$deferrals),
  state = vapply(plan$deferrals, `[[`, character(1), 'state'),
  detail = vapply(plan$deferrals, `[[`, character(1), 'detail'),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

The plan only proposes the enrollment. `apply` records it and writes the healthy
operations:

```{r enroll-apply}
invisible(specmill::generate_client(
  root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply', deferrals = enroll
))
list.files(file.path(root, 'R'))
```

`demo_good.R` and `demo_health.R` exist. There is no `demo_bad.R`, and no
placeholder for it either. The manifest now holds the enrollment:

```{r manifest}
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(root, '.specmill/manifest.json'))
str(manifest$deferrals)
```

The `fingerprint` is a SHA-256 of the operation and every local definition it
references. It is what lets specmill tell a real contract change from noise. From
now on `check` passes and reports the operation as deferred:

```{r deferred-check}
checked <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'check')
vapply(checked$deferrals, `[[`, character(1), 'state')
```

### The contract changes but is still broken

An edit to the operation changes its fingerprint, so specmill retries it. Here
upstream adds prose to `GET /bad` but still omits the response description:

```{r still-blocked}
lines <- readLines(file.path(root, 'api.yml'))
lines <- sub(
  'operationId: bad', 'operationId: bad\n      description: Now with prose', lines
)
writeLines(lines, file.path(root, 'api.yml'))
plan <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
plan$deferrals[[1]]
```

`retry_blocked` still needs a decision: fix it, enroll it again with a new
reason, or exclude it. Edits to *unrelated* operations do not wake the
enrollment.

### The contract is fixed

Now upstream supplies the description:

```{r recovered}
write_schema(bad_description = 'OK')
plan <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
plan$deferrals[[1]]
vapply(plan$operations, `[[`, character(1), 'id')
```

`retry_recovered` means the operation now passes. The plan already shows the new
wrapper. `apply` writes it through the normal gates and drops the enrollment:

```{r recovered-apply}
invisible(specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply'))
list.files(file.path(root, 'R'))
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(root, '.specmill/manifest.json'))
length(manifest$deferrals)
```

To retry an operation without waiting for a contract change, clear it
explicitly with `deferrals = list(clear = 'demo GET /bad')`. A toolkit update
alone never wakes an enrollment.

To enroll failures automatically, add
`deferral: {automatic: [schema_validation_invalid]}` to the service. See
[Automatic contract-change deferral](configuration.html#automatic-contract-change-deferral).

## 5. Skip

Skipping is a different decision. You are saying you do not want this operation
wrapped, whatever its contract looks like. Add an `exclude` regex to the service:

```{r exclude}
writeLines(
  c(readLines(file.path(root, 'service.yml')), 'selection:', "  exclude: ['^/health']"),
  file.path(root, 'service.yml')
)
plan <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
excluded <- plan$excluded[[1]]
unlist(excluded[c('id', 'status', 'classification', 'reason', 'guidance')])
```

An excluded operation is listed in the inventory but its schema is never
validated. Unlike a deferral, exclusion plans to remove an existing wrapper:

```{r exclude-files}
data.frame(
  file = vapply(plan$files, function(x) basename(x$file), character(1)),
  action = vapply(plan$files, `[[`, character(1), 'action')
)
```

The `remove` row is `demo_health.R`. Removal needs verified ownership, so a file
you edited by hand is protected instead. Review it in plan before you apply.

## 6. Which one to use

| Situation | Choose |
|---|---|
| Upstream is expected to fix a single operation, and you have a working wrapper you must keep | Defer |
| You never want the operation wrapped, for example a health check | Skip |
| You control the schema copy and can correct it | Fix, then plan again |
| The whole document fails validation, or a file is unreadable | None of these. Fix the document first. |

For the full state table and its limits, return to
[Routine maintenance and CI](maintenance.html#defer-a-changed-contract-that-does-not-validate-yet).
For selection policy, see [Configuration](configuration.html#exclude-methods-without-editing-endpoint-lists).
